key_insight: KANs can predict airfoil pressure distributions well and interpolate across Mach number and angle of attack, but they do not clearly outperform a well-tuned MLP and are outperformed by a GNN in this study.
engineering_relevance: For aerodynamic surrogate modeling, KANs offer a lower-complexity, faster-training alternative that may be useful when model efficiency matters, but accuracy gains over established networks are not guaranteed.
method: Compared KAN, MLP, and GNN surrogate models for surface pressure prediction on subsonic and transonic airfoils.
Evaluated the ability to predict full pressure-coefficient distributions and interpolate across Mach numbers and angles of attack.
Assessed accuracy versus model complexity and training cost.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that KAN performance was comparable but slightly below a suitably trained MLP, while the best results came from a GNN at the cost of longer training.
watch_item: KAN training is sensitive to hyperparameter choice and can exhibit instability, so careful tuning is necessary before deployment.
paper_title: Kolmogorov Arnold networks (KAN) for aerodynamic prediction: a comparison with MLPs and GNNs
